For game, it's not enabled by default, for editor, we can add a setting to disable it, and also we need to disable it manually when it causes noise for some editor classes.

> Is it possible to remove this option? It's not enabled by default for editor theme now, I have enabled it manually for the classes that has many columns and no collapsing and adjusted the editor theme guide color for dark/light themes.

Why is `draw_color_lines` an integer and doesn't allow a color to be chosen like https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89890? It's somewhat true that one can get an acceptable value automatically, but the choice is important for most users and developers alike.
Regardless, my personal consensus is still the same as https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89890#issuecomment-2020262693

> Why is `draw_color_lines` an integer and doesn't allow a color to be chosen like #89890? It's somewhat true that one can get an acceptable value automatically, but the choice is important for most users and developers alike. Regardless, my personal consensus is still the same as [#89890 (comment)](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/89890#issuecomment-2020262693) It's using the `guide_color` by default, also it's useful for trees with more than one column like the `Video RAM` tree. Edit: `draw_color_guides` is to enable/disable the feature, and the `guide_color` controls both the line guides and the new color rect guides color.

This shows how it will look for editor `FileSystem` and `SceneTree`.

> Are these color guide colors exposed though style boxes when users add their own Tree nodes and style them? I couldn't find this out quickly in my test project.

It's just drawing a semi-transparent rect for each even row using the same guide lines color in theme properties.

> IMO from what I checked the ones you already applied this to seem fine

Agreed, it's most useful for multi-column trees. Maybe editor shortcuts need stripes too

> It's just drawing a semi-transparent rect for each even row using the same guide lines color in theme properties.

Any chance they could be styleboxes? It would be handy to be able to draw them with rounded corners, including in editor

> I also agree that this should be disabled by default.

This is probably a matter of preference but I think having them enabled is a better default and they slightly improve readability with multiple columns

> Agreed, it's most useful for multi-column trees. Maybe editor shortcuts need stripes too I tried that before, but it ended up being somewhat confusing for foldable trees. > Any chance they could be styleboxes? It would be handy to be able to draw them with rounded corners, including in editor Right now this can be enabled with a single line of code `tree->add_theme_constant_override("draw_color_guides", 1)` If we switch to using styleboxes, managing this becomes more complicated. Most styleboxes are disabled by default using `EmptyStyleBox`, so to keep the current default behavior we would need the default stylebox to remain empty. Enabling it in the editor would then have to be handled by the editor theme, which would likely enable it for all Tree instances by default. The alternative would be creating a type variation specifically for this feature so it can still be enabled easily. Otherwise, if we keep it disabled by default using the theme constant `draw_color_guides` instead of empty style, users might set the stylebox and see no visible change, which could be confusing. > This is probably a matter of preference but I think having them enabled is a better default and they slightly improve readability with multiple columns In my opinion it doesn’t look very good for trees with many foldable children, and it can also look awkward for trees that only have a single column. Because of that, it’s probably better to evaluate the visual impact across these different cases before deciding on changing the default behavior.

> Right now this can be enabled with a single line of code
tree->add_theme_constant_override("draw_color_guides", 1)
If we switch to using styleboxes, managing this becomes more complicated. Most styleboxes are disabled by default using EmptyStyleBox, so to keep the current default behavior we would need the default stylebox to remain empty.

Right now the guides can be customized with a single color. This could be changed to a StyleBox, separately from `draw_color_guides`, which would still toggle it.

I also wonder if `draw_color_guides` should even be a theme property if it's not something you'd want to have consistently enabled/disabled for every tree. Could be a regular property.

> I also wonder if `draw_color_guides` should even be a theme property if it's not something you'd want to have consistently enabled/disabled for every tree. Could be a regular property. Changed it to be a property named `alternate_rows_visible` (disabled by default), and it draws a rounded corner stylebox now by default for both modern and classic themes. Edit: I will fill the stylebox docs after passing the checks.
Rebased. Thanks for testing the new changes.
The new GDExtension tab in Project Settings should also have this enabled.

`alternate_row_style_visible` ?

Edit:
`alternate_rows` may also work if anyone prefers short names.

Is it correct that this isn't applied to Trees like the FileSystem and the SceneTree view by default? I've tried this PR and while I do see the option for enabling alternating lines for Tress I make in the engine, I can't find anyway to actually enable this for these editor views in particular, which is what I most was looking forward to. I understand that the usability of this mostly comes from when it's a multi-column type of Tree, but I do think there's a certain level of added "niceness" in having stripes for even simple views. Blender for instance isn't much bigger than how I have mine setup in Godot, and while the effect is much more subtle than the proposed look here, not to be greedy or anything, but I would be appreciative of a toggle that allowed for it, and if not that's okay too. Unless of course there already is, in which case I'm surely blind because I cannot seem to find anything alluding to it in either the code or the editor settings :sweat: As for the naming of the property... while I don't believe I'm any source of authority, I'm partial towards `alternate_row_style_visible`, I don't think prefixing with `use_` makes sense, given the context of the other property just above (`column_titles_visible`), which is functionally similar to the alternate row property, and doesn't have `use_`. Would be inconsistent, I think.

My problem with `alternate_rows_visible` is that it's ambiguous. It may be interpreted as a toggle for the whole rows, not the style. Something that better describes it visually would be better IMO, like `stripes_visible` even.

It's just a suggestion though, going with the current name is ok too 🤷‍♂️

`alternate_item_background_style`
`alternate_item_backgrounds`

I think `striped_rows` is more descriptive than `alternate_rows`.

`striped_rows_visible` for the property.
`striped_rows_background` for the theme stylebox property.

Renamed the property to `row_stripes_visible` to match `column_titles_visible` name style.

> Is it correct that this isn't applied to Trees like the `FileSystem` and the `SceneTree` view by default? I've tried this PR and while I do see the option for enabling alternating lines for Tress I make in the engine, I can't find anyway to actually enable this for these editor views in particular, which is what I most was looking forward to.

Hello, I have added an option in EditorSettings `docks/scene_tree/show_row_stripes` to allow enabling this new feature for scene tree dock.

For `EditorFileSystem`, it can be added later, since it doesn't go well with folder background colors.

> Hello, I have added an option in EditorSettings `docks/scene_tree/show_row_stripes` to allow enabling this new feature for scene tree dock. > > For `EditorFileSystem`, it can be added later, since it doesn't go well with folder background colors. I've been using this PR for a couple weeks now and this has very much helped with readability with the scene tree, thank you. However, I have ran into an issue regarding the color of it, as with certain background colors the alternate row becomes completely invisible, and with the background color I normally use (#1e1e2e) it is quite hard to see. I'm not entirely sure how this should be handled as I'm not sure if a new color setting in the editor theme settings is something desirable. With a fully black background, or otherwise referred to as the "OLED" theme, the stripe has no actual appearance. Additionally, this may seem a bit nit picky, but for both the editor and the actual theme usage of this, would it be possible to have an option or way of extending the alternate row through out the entirety of the panel? As seen in Blender, I find this to be a more visually pleasing approach as it gives the look that each alternating row is a "slot" so to speak for something to go inside of it, I'm not sure how many people actually care about this sort of thing so I understand if it's not something you want to do. (And perhaps it could be something I can look into otherwise) I once again thank you for your work, and I hope to see this new style option become used elsewhere in the editor in the future, especially with the FileSystem dock. --- I went ahead and modified this to allow an alternate_row_color within interface/theme It does feel slightly overkill having a new color option here, but given it's mostly a readability/accessibility feature perhaps it's okay? As an aside, I think the alternate rows, specifically within the tree view, are visually better if the rounded corners are removed. Here's what a catppuccin-like theme would look like before and after colored alternate rows and no rounded corners. A minor difference, but when the tree view is at the corner of a screen where the color is slightly shifted, it actually does help quite a bit. If this is something desirable I can add presets for each theme (currently all just empty) and give you a .patch
@WhalesState Is the above comment something you're interested in integrating? The PR will need a rebase anyway, so it'd probably be worth a look

Yes, the current dark theme alpha value is `0.025` which only works with darkest colors, I'll need to adjust it somehow based on theme `base_color` or we allow the users to adjust it with a slider. I can rebase it tomorrow then we test it with different theme colors to find the best alpha value for dark themes or we allow adjusting it from editor theme settings.
